mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW Z1 25i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full BMW Z1 25i engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£6,000 supply-only for a rebuilt M20B25 unit, or £4,000-£6,500 fitted by a specialist. Used M20B25 engines: £1,200-£2,500 depending on mileage and condition. Reconditioned units: £2,200-£4,000. Professional fitting adds £1,000-£2,000 to the engine cost.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW Z1 25i M20B25 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M20B25 is one of BMW's most robust and characterful straight-six engines, shared with the E30 325i. However, Z1-specific issues exist: the unique cylinder-head oil-feed restriction starves the valvetrain on 1989-1991 models, and the under-body exhaust heat-shield failure cooks starter motors. The Z1 sits 40mm lower than the E30, flattening the sump angle and causing oil starvation at low RPM - a fault never seen in the E30. Regular maintenance, particularly timing belt replacement every 60,000 miles, is essential.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing belt failure in a BMW Z1 25i M20B25?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M20B25 uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced every 60,000 miles or 5 years. Warning signs include: no warning - the belt typically snaps without prior symptoms; rattling or squealing noise from the front of the engine; engine misfire or loss of power if belt has jumped a tooth; complete engine seizure - if the belt snaps, pistons strike valves.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW Z1 25i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Z1 25i worth £20,000-£50,000, a £2,500-£5,000 rebuilt engine is typically good value - replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable up to approximately 70% of the car's value. Given the vehicle's collector-car status, specialist rebuild with warranty is the safest option. Always factor the 12-month warranty into your replacement decision.

mainEntity.name: What causes the BMW Z1 25i M20B25 oil starvation problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Z1 sits 40mm lower than the E30 325i, which flattens the sump angle and alters oil pickup geometry. This causes oil starvation at low RPM, leading to camshaft lobe pitting and wear - a fault never seen in the E30. Symptoms include ticking or tapping from the top end. Camshaft pitting is visible on inspection. The fix is an up-rated oil pump (OEM 11 41 1 730 302) and hardened 731 camshaft.

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my BMW Z1 25i engine with a different engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine swaps to a different size or type are technically complex and rarely cost-effective for the Z1 25i. The M20B25 is the only engine fitted to the Z1 from the factory - stick to like-for-like replacement. Swapping to an M50 or S50 requires different ECU, wiring, engine mounts, and transmission. The Z1's unique chassis and low ride height make non-standard swaps extremely difficult. Insurance must be notified of any non-standard engine swap. Our marketplace only recommends like-for-like code-matching for warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW Z1 25i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW Z1 25i arrived in 1989 as BMW's first dedicated roadster since the 507, powered exclusively by the M20B25 2.5-litre straight-six from the E30 325i. With just 8,000 units produced between 1989 and 1991, the Z1 is one of the rarest BMW models ever built - and the sole drivetrain specification remained unchanged throughout its brief production run.

milestones.description: March 1989 - BMW Z1 25i production begins with the M20B25 2.5-litre straight-six petrol engine, producing 170hp and 222Nm of torque
1991 - Z1 production continues with the M20B25 engine unchanged; all UK-market cars are left-hand drive
June 1991 - Z1 production ends after 8,000 units; no engine changes were made during the production run

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW Z1 25i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

problems.rootCause: The M20B25 uses a rubber timing belt rather than a chain. If the belt breaks, pistons strike valves - catastrophic engine failure requiring full replacement. The belt should be replaced every 60,000 miles or 5 years, whichever comes first.

With a full rebuilt engine costing £2,500-£5,000 fitted, replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value - making engine replacement a financially viable option for most Z1 owners. problems.rootCause: The Z1's under-body exhaust heat shield fails over time, allowing exhaust heat to cook the starter motor. This Z1-specific issue is not seen on E30 325i models due to different exhaust routing.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace starter motor, inspect heat shield

problems.recommendation: If your Z1 25i suffers from hot-start issues or the starter motor fails, check the exhaust heat shield first. A £200-£350 starter motor replacement is a quick fix, but without replacing the heat shield, the problem will recur. On a collector car, it's worth spending the extra £150-£250 to replace the heat shield at the same time.
